title: Many and One: one maker, the vacant centre and Theophrastus at the joint
description: The papers on this page argue that the Plato–Aristotle corpus is the work of one person divided by voice, object and name: Many and One (#1575, August 2026) holds that what made him look like many authors is that he wrote about many things and that Socrates not writing is the form of the vacant centre, and states an open falsification programme. The Notebook (#1569) argues κερματισμός across four loci and the just/unjust argument relabelled as weaker/stronger, and holds its lexical battery tracks period, not pupillage. EA-CORPORA-14 (#1595) argues Theophrastus's fragment holds the position of the question and Λ of the attempt; later claims narrow this to one locus (#1601), widen it to nine loci (#1602) and the whole fragment (#1667), then narrow it to eight locations in one stretch (#1605). #1658 carries the reading to memory at De anima III.5. EA-CORPORA-05 (#1560) specifies a Pessoa hold-out, which its erratum (#1561) corrects to an analytical one. The page also holds an unrelated claim on Sophocles.

claims.statement:
**ONE PERSON WROTE THIS.** That is the claim of this paper, and nothing
above dissolves, replaces, or spiritualises it.

**⚠ And "person" is not here defined as "one body."** The paper does not require the maker to be individuated biologically, and §§I–V have spent five sections showing that what counts as one depends on the mode of unity. **What is claimed is that however the maker is divided — by voice, by object, by name, by position — the divisions are of ONE PERSON and not an aggregation of several.**
claims.falsifier: Only one of them can be checked against the text by the corpus-internal methods used here; the other asks how many embodied makers there were, and that question lives in the external record — papyrology [VIII.4], inscriptions, transmission history — which this paper does not touch.**

So: one thing, many true accounts, and the many are a defect of sight only when they are taken for many things.

Where the fragment says an account is needed, Λ supplies one; where it says the astronomers' account will not do, Λ 8 is the astronomers' account. note especially that the Theophrastan text's demand at 5 a 21 — *the cause of the number of the spheres seeks a greater account, and not the astronomers'* — is answered in *Metaphysics* Λ 8 by the astronomers' account, offered with the concession *let the necessity be left for stronger minds to state*. Two texts, one demand, one supply, and no way to determine from the sequence alone which was written first.

**Established, and independent of everything in this note:** the textual correspondences between Λ and *On First Principles* at the loci treated separately — S1 through S9, with the sphere-count at 5 a 21-3 ‖ Λ 8 as the sharpest. Those are relations between passages, verified against van Raalte's margins, and they do not depend on any account of biography, catalogue or chronology.

**All of it is draft material, excised, and all of it has a place.** The fragment is therefore taken *entire* — all 3,370 words, in its own received order, nothing omitted and nothing moved — and Λ is spliced in wherever the fragment's argument calls for an account it does not give.
statements.falsifier: **Does not show:** how many hands wrote them, when either was composed, or that any demand precedes its supply in time. The three counters stand at full strength: aporetic demands are ordinarily raised against a standing position; both texts may draw on a discussion we do not have; priority in inquiry is not priority in composition.

statements.quote: **What it claims.** That the two passages stand in ordered textual dependency at eight locations within a continuous 382-word stretch; that the order is fixed by the passage's own connectives — *τούτων* pointing back, *τὸ δὲ μετὰ ταῦτα* forward, *ἀφ᾽ ἧς* twice requiring its immediate antecedent; and that at 5a21–23 the object, the science, the demand and the shortfall converge.
